chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shamoun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asamm, from Misma', from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Ali (peace be upon him) judged regarding the ear lobe, [assigning] one-third of the wergild of the ear.
And by the first chain, regarding the two ears, if one of them is cut, its wergild is five hundred dinars, and whatever is cut from it is calculated accordingly.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling and financial compensation for cutting an ear or ear lobe?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi details the precise financial compensation (diyah) for ear injuries, establishing the ear lobe's value at one-third of the total and setting the full wergild for one ear at five hundred dinars. It reflects the systematic application of proportional calculation (bi-hisab dhalika) in Shia jurisprudence for partial damages, ensuring equitable restitution based on the severity of the injury.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Muhammad Bin Al Hassan Bin Shamoun, from Abdullah Bin Abdul Rahman Al Asamma, from Misma’a, 
Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘Ali<sup>asws</sup> judged regarding an ear lobe, being one-third of the wergild of the ear’.
And by the first chain regarding the two ears when one of them is cut, so its wergild is five hundred Dinars, and whatever is cut from it, it would be by the accounting of that’.
